card.name: Endings of cardiovascular and intra-arterial
card.fires_on: The word ending partway through long medical terms, mainly "ULAR" in CARDIOVASCULAR, "ial" in intra-arterial and "ory" in excretory. Most common in capitalized warning headings and dosage section titles.

modes.label: CARDIOVASCULAR in caps
modes.description: The "ULAR" ending of CARDIOVASCULAR in boxed warning headings.
modes.example: RISK OF SERIOUS CARDIOVASCULAR AND GASTROINTESTINAL EVENTS . WARNING: RISK OF SERIOUS CARDIOVASC<<ULAR>> AND GASTROINTESTINAL EVENTS

modes.label: Intra-arterial endings
modes.description: The ending or middle piece of intra-arterial in dosage headings.
modes.example: 230 mL 2.4 Recommended Dosage for Intra-arter<<ial>> and Intravenous Procedures in Pediatric Patients The

modes.label: Other route or procedure words
modes.description: Endings of words like excretory in procedure names.
modes.example: Body Weight to Administer Excret<<ory>> Urography 300

card.writes: It pushes toward unrelated Chinese phrases and away from medical words like medical, medically and health, so it adds no clear medical output.
card.plain: It lights up when a long medical word like cardiovascular or intra-arterial is nearly finished.
